newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle trade thin at $69 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle trade thin at $69 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle traded in light volume at $69.00 per cwt, steady with Thursday's active sales, going into the long Labor Day holiday weekend, feedlot sources said.
With most packers closed on Monday in observance of Labor Day, trading was not expected to get underway in force again until at least Wednesday next week, the sources said.
By then, packers will be able to detect how well beef moved out of supermarket meat cases over the long weekend and adjust cattle buying plans accordingly, they said.

Boxed beef prices this week have fallen steadily, with midday prices quoted down $0.68 to $1.03 per cwt, according to USDA. The value of choice, yield-grade 3 carcasses weighing 700- to 850-lbs has dropped $4.07 since last Friday when the slide began.
If beef prices continue to weaken after the holiday, it could offset potential support to fed cattle prices linked to tight supplies of market-ready cattle, cattle feeders said.
